title: Space motion sickness: nausea and vomiting

differential.label: Space motion sickness
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. Most likely in the first days of flight.

differential.label: Dehydration from vomiting
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. Can follow any cause of vomiting.

differential.label: Stomach or gut infection
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. Fever or diarrhea makes this more likely.

differential.label: High cabin CO2
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis. Nausea has been reported at high CO2 levels.

differential.label: Head injury or radiation sickness. Cannot be ruled out onboard. Needs flight surgeon review
differential.note: Working idea only. This is not a diagnosis.

tests.title: Sickness grade
tests.instruction: Pick one grade. Mild: few symptoms, at most one vomit. Moderate: lasting symptoms, no more than 2 vomits. Severe: more than 2 vomits or cannot work.

tests.title: Vomiting count
tests.instruction: Count every time the person vomits. Write down the count and the time.

tests.title: Heart rate
tests.instruction: Stay restrained. Read heart rate on the blood pressure monitor and enter it.

tests.title: Systolic blood pressure
tests.instruction: Stay restrained. Read systolic blood pressure on the monitor and enter it.

tests.title: Diastolic blood pressure
tests.instruction: Stay restrained. Read diastolic blood pressure on the monitor and enter it.

tests.title: Body temperature
tests.instruction: Take a temperature with the oral thermometer and enter it.

immediateSteps.title: Restrain your body and keep your head still
immediateSteps.instruction: Strap in or hold a rail. Keep your head still. Avoid nodding movements.

immediateSteps.title: Close your eyes or focus on one task
immediateSteps.instruction: Close your eyes. Or focus on one simple task.

immediateSteps.title: Get away from smells and heat
immediateSteps.instruction: Move away from strong smells. Move away from warm spots.

immediateSteps.title: Sip fluids
immediateSteps.instruction: Take small sips of water if you can keep them down.

immediateSteps.title: Count vomiting episodes
immediateSteps.instruction: Record each vomit and the time.

immediateSteps.title: Do not start an EVA or critical task
immediateSteps.instruction: Tell the commander. Hold any spacewalk or critical task.

immediateSteps.title: Send the case to the flight surgeon
immediateSteps.instruction: Continue to handoff and send the case. The flight surgeon decides on treatment with you.

cautions: This card is not a diagnosis. It gives no doses. Treatment is decided by the crew together with the flight surgeon. Motion sickness medicines can cause drowsiness. Use any kit item only as the flight surgeon directs.
sourceNote: Researcher card, Pulseframe Batch 1, 2026-11-15. Built from NASA OCHMO-MTB-004 Rev A (Space Adaptation Sickness), NASA IMM data and MedlinePlus. Not a NASA procedure. Pending second-person safety review.
redFlagsLifeThreat: Blood or dark coffee-ground material in the vomit.
Confusion, or the person is hard to wake.
redFlagsCallGround: Cannot keep fluids down for 12 hours.
Fever or diarrhea with the vomiting.

timeLimits.item: Mild sickness usually clears in 36 to 48 hours.
Moderate sickness usually clears in 72 hours.
Severe sickness may last past 72 hours. Call the flight surgeon.
No fluids kept down for 12 hours, or vomiting past 24 hours: call the flight surgeon.

whenGroundUnavailable.status: PARTIAL (historical rule found, no current rule)
whenGroundUnavailable.detail: The 2001 ISS medical checklist says that in an emergency or during loss of signal the crew begins treatment, then calls the surgeon as soon as possible. This is a 2001 rule. No current public NASA or ESA rule was found. No public NASA procedure covers motion sickness treatment without ground contact. MTB-004 says treatment is decided by crew with the flight surgeon, and ISS schedules daily private medical conferences for the first five days. Looked in: OCHMO-MTB-004, OCHMO-TB-006, HRP 2017 evidence report.
firstAidThatNeedsNoGround: Keep the head still and the body restrained.
Record vomit count, heart rate, blood pressure and temperature with times.
Send the case as soon as the link returns.
